name: Frontend Modules Registry
tagline: Provides API endpoint for dynamic frontend module discovery via Module Federation. Replaces static apps.json.

readme.overview: VirtoCommerce.ModuleFederation scans installed .NET module manifests for `<frontendModules>` declarations, resolves which modules belong to which host apps via the dependency graph, and serves a runtime API that host apps use to load remote MF bundles. **Key properties:** - Modules are host-agnostic — they declare capabilities, not consumers - .NET dependency graph provides intelligent defaults (Recommended modules) - All other compatible modules are visible as Available for manual activation - Admin has final control over which modules are enabled per app - Installing a .NET module auto-enables its frontend extensions for related apps

notes.forAnalyst: The registry that lets independently built front-end modules load into one admin application at runtime.
notes.forArchitect: No dependencies, one entity, four migrations — and it lives in the `frontend-modules` repository, which is why its registry ProjectUrl redirects. It is the back-end half of the admin UI's Module Federation setup.
notes.forDeveloper: Register a remote and the shell loads it at runtime; version skew between shell and remote is the failure mode to design against. Pair it with the platform's Module federation atom.
reachForItWhen: The back office must be extended by separately deployed front-end modules
Teams need to ship UI without rebuilding the shell
A remote's version has to be recorded rather than assumed
doNotReachForItWhen: A single, monolithic admin build is acceptable — this adds moving parts
The extension is server-side: this is front-end composition
Shell and remote cannot be kept version-compatible
